forces.title: Travel planning shifts to fragmented, always-on 'orbit' customer journey
forces.description: The customer journey for travel has transformed from a linear path to a dynamic, non-linear 'orbit.' Inspiration is now continuous and ubiquitous through social media and AI, making booking decisions provisional. This increases touchpoints but also creates fragmentation, requiring travel players to adapt by focusing on sustained engagement and building trust throughout the iterative planning process.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Fragmented research creates 'restart tax,' increasing churn risk for travel operators
forces.description: Travelers face significant friction due to fragmented research across numerous, disconnected platforms (search, AI, OTAs, reviews, supplier sites). This lack of context sharing leads to a 'restart tax,' forcing consumers to re-enter preferences and re-validate decisions, increasing frustration. This unsolved industry problem raises the risk of travelers abandoning one trip orbit for another that seems easier to plan.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: AI's growing role in travel planning creates opportunities despite trust gap
forces.description: AI is rapidly emerging as a powerful tool for travel inspiration and itinerary generation, with 71% of travelers comfortable using it for inspiration and 86% considering it for bookings. While traveler confidence in AI for final booking lags, its ability to quickly narrow options and provide detailed plans offers a significant opportunity for operators to enhance discovery, personalize experiences, and potentially streamline parts of the customer journey.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Rising consumer desire for self-expression through travel fuels discretionary spending
forces.description: Travel is increasingly viewed as a form of self-expression, with 68% of travelers stating trips are part of their identity. This trend drives significant discretionary spending, especially among younger demographics (52% of Gen Z and 47% of Millennials splurge on experiences). This fundamental shift in traveler motivation provides a strong tailwind for consumer services, encouraging premium offerings and unique experiences.
forces.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

forces.title: Global wellness economy growth creates tailwinds for leisure and hospitality
forces.description: The global wellness economy is projected to grow approximately 8% annually through 2030, outpacing many other discretionary categories. Consumers are expanding their definition of wellness to include holistic wellbeing, leading to increased spending on nutrition, fitness experiences, and wellness services. This structural shift provides a strong tailwind for the Travel, Tourism & Leisure segment (especially the wellness sub-segment) and can open new opportunities for hotels and other service providers.
forces.source_title: As Wellness Spending Grows, Can Activewear Brands Seize the Opportunity?

forces.title: Indian events and experiences sector transforming into high-impact economic catalyst
forces.description: India's events and experiences industry is evolving from a fragmented collection of businesses into a dynamic service ecosystem, driven by urbanization, rising incomes, and digital adoption. It now encompasses diverse organized experiences like MICE, live entertainment, and sports, creating significant multiplier effects across hospitality, travel, and local economies. This transformation positions the sector as a strategic lever for growth, tourism, employment, and India's 'orange economy' ambitions.
forces.source_title: Socio-economic impact of the Indian events and experiences industry

forces.title: Events industry drives high-value tourism from outstation visitors, boosting local economies
forces.description: Events, especially MICE and large-format concerts, are significant drivers of destination travel, with a majority (54.4%) of attendees traveling from outside their city. These outstation visitors spend 2-3 times more per day than leisure tourists on travel, accommodation, dining, and shopping. This concentrated demand creates a substantial 'halo effect' for host cities, generating economic activity and supporting local businesses beyond the event venue itself.
forces.source_title: Socio-economic impact of the Indian events and experiences industry

forces.title: Regulatory complexities and infrastructure gaps hinder events sector growth potential
forces.description: Despite its significant economic potential, the Indian events and experiences industry faces challenges from complex regulatory frameworks, inadequate event-ready infrastructure, and insufficient social protection for its large contractual and gig workforce. Streamlined, single-window clearances, continued investment in Tier 2/3 infrastructure, strengthened skilling pathways, and clearer guidance on crowd safety are crucial for the sector to realize its full growth and employment generation capabilities.
forces.source_title: Socio-economic impact of the Indian events and experiences industry

forces.title: Resilient macroeconomic growth supports overall consumer discretionary spending
forces.description: India's projected real GDP growth of 6.7% for FY27, coupled with RBI's efforts to stabilize the rupee and attract capital, creates a supportive macroeconomic environment. This resilience translates into sustained consumer spending capacity, providing a crucial tailwind for the Consumer Services industry, which relies heavily on discretionary income. Although global uncertainties persist, the weakening linkage between monsoon and economic growth further enhances stability.

forces.title: Heritage tourism driven by demand for immersive, authentic, tech-enabled experiences
forces.description: Heritage tourism is undergoing a significant transformation, moving from conventional sightseeing to 'story living,' with travelers demanding immersive, authentic, and tech-enabled experiences. This shift is fueled by Gen Z and millennials who prioritize cultural immersion, learning, and sustainability. Leveraging technologies like AR/VR and AI, alongside curated cultural programming and community engagement, is crucial for destinations to enhance competitiveness and increase visitor spending and repeat visitation.
forces.source_title: Heritage reimagined: Driving immersive, tech-enabled and experience-led tourism

forces.title: Strong government policy support and investment accelerate tourism infrastructure development
forces.description: Government initiatives like Swadesh Darshan 2.0 and PRASHAD, along with significant capital allocations (e.g., Union Budget focus on thematic trails, medical tourism hubs), are strengthening India's tourism infrastructure. This policy support and investment are crucial for enhancing connectivity, developing sustainable destinations, and improving visitor experiences across various tourism segments, creating a robust foundation for long-term growth in consumer services.
forces.source_title: Tourism And Hospitality Industry In India

forces.title: Domestic tourism serves as cornerstone for India's hospitality growth and regional development
forces.description: Domestic tourism contributes nearly 88% of total tourism spending in India and is projected to continue growing strongly, fueled by younger demographics and higher disposable incomes. This robust internal demand, coupled with urban Indians' preference for shorter, experience-led breaks, drives infrastructure development and opens new markets in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. This makes domestic tourism a foundational tailwind for the hospitality sector, ensuring resilience and expanding reach.
forces.source_title: Tourism And Hospitality Industry In India

forces.title: Emerging niche tourism segments drive specialized growth and diversify offerings
forces.description: India is witnessing strong growth in specialized tourism segments such as rural, spiritual, eco-tourism, luxury, adventure, medical, cruise, and camping. These emerging areas attract varied traveler segments, including high-spending tourists (e.g., luxury and medical tourism), and are supported by government promotions and infrastructure development. This diversification broadens the revenue streams and market opportunities for consumer services beyond traditional travel and hospitality.
forces.source_title: Tourism And Hospitality Industry In India

forces.title: GST reduction on hotel stays boosts domestic travel and hospitality sector growth
forces.description: The reduction of GST on hotel stays under Rs. 7,500 to 5% is a significant policy tailwind expected to fuel robust growth in India's hospitality sector. This measure directly reduces costs for consumers, making hotel accommodations more affordable and incentivizing domestic travel. It is projected to play a key role in boosting occupancy rates and contributing to India's ambition of reaching a US$ 1 trillion hotel industry contribution to GDP by 2047.
forces.source_title: Tourism And Hospitality Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Travel planning shifts from linear path to dynamic 'orbit' model, requiring continuous engagement
viewpoints.description: The travel customer journey has evolved from a linear path to a 'looping orbit,' driven by always-on inspiration from social media and AI. This creates numerous entry points but also fragmentation and a 'restart tax' for travelers. Operators must adapt by focusing on continuous engagement, building trust, and integrating context across platforms to reduce friction. Success depends on making return visits easier than starting fresh, as booking decisions are less final than before.
viewpoints.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

viewpoints.title: Increased competition in travel inspiration necessitates trust and authentic customer feedback
viewpoints.description: The proliferation of digital channels (OTAs, search, social, AI) has created more 'front doors' for travel inspiration, intensifying competition. Accor believes that trust, not just inspiration, drives conversion. Surfacing genuine customer feedback, including imperfections, and user-generated content, builds confidence more effectively than curated brand narratives. Empowering staff to create memorable, human-centric experiences is crucial, as these moments generate relatable content that fosters upstream influence.
viewpoints.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

viewpoints.title: Operators must adapt to inspiration shifting to social/AI platforms, not owned channels
viewpoints.description: Travel inspiration is increasingly occurring on social media and AI platforms, not direct operator channels, leading customers to arrive 'further down the decision funnel.' Operators should not rush to close sales, but rather extend the inspiration at the handoff moment. Landing pages need to pick up the traveler's narrative, provide relatable imagery and reviews, and enable flexible exploration rather than forcing immediate booking, allowing travelers to orbit ideas without full commitment.
viewpoints.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

viewpoints.title: Industry lacks continuity across travel platforms, causing 'restart tax' for consumers
viewpoints.description: The travel industry has failed to solve continuity across diverse platforms and devices, resulting in travelers frequently restarting their research journeys. This 'restart tax' makes it easier for consumers to abandon one trip idea for another, as inspiration is always frictionless while research is not. Marriott emphasizes the need for interfaces to interpret intent, provide verified data, and preserve context across sessions to make returning easier than starting over.
viewpoints.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

viewpoints.title: Wellness spending provides significant growth opportunity for consumer services
viewpoints.description: The global wellness economy is experiencing robust growth, outpacing many other discretionary categories, creating strong tailwinds for related consumer services. Consumers are expanding their definition of wellness beyond exercise to holistic well-being, driving increased spending across adjacent categories like nutrition, fitness experiences, and wellness services. This presents a key opportunity for travel, tourism, and leisure operators (especially those in fitness centers, wellness sub_segment) to capitalize on this momentum by tailoring offerings and building credibility in adjacencies.
viewpoints.source_title: As Wellness Spending Grows, Can Activewear Brands Seize the Opportunity?

viewpoints.title: India's events and experiences industry is a high-impact economic catalyst at inflection point
viewpoints.description: India’s events and experiences industry is a rapidly expanding economic and social contributor, driving consumption, tourism, employment, and community engagement. It exhibits a strong multiplier effect across hospitality, travel, retail, and logistics. The sector is undergoing transformation due to digital technologies, AI, hybrid formats, and sustainability focus. To unlock its full potential, supportive ecosystems, including streamlined regulations, investment in infrastructure, and workforce protection, are crucial for continued growth and global positioning.
viewpoints.source_title: Socio-economic impact of the Indian events and experiences industry

viewpoints.title: Experience economy drives urban growth and tourism, necessitating data-driven investment
viewpoints.description: India’s experience economy is a significant and measurable driver of urban growth, tourism, small business activity, and services employment. Events create a 'halo effect' that boosts spending in transport, accommodation, and visitor-facing sectors beyond the event venue. Leveraging aggregated and anonymized spending data, as demonstrated by the Mastercard Economics Institute, can inform public-sector decisions, enabling targeted investment in infrastructure, digital acceptance, destination promotion, and overall visitor experience to unlock lasting benefits.
viewpoints.source_title: Socio-economic impact of the Indian events and experiences industry

viewpoints.title: India's macroeconomic resilience supports consumer spending despite global uncertainties
viewpoints.description: Despite geopolitical volatility (US-Iran conflict impacting crude oil) and monsoon concerns, India's macroeconomic resilience is expected to sustain. Strong GDP growth (projected 6.7% for FY27 by CareEdge) and RBI's aggressive interventions to stabilize the rupee and attract capital flows are positive indicators. While state fiscal pressures exist, the overall economic environment suggests continued consumer spending capacity, which is crucial for the discretionary consumer services sector.

viewpoints.title: Nutraceutical industry positioned for long-term growth driven by health awareness
viewpoints.description: India’s nutraceutical industry is projected for sustained long-term growth (10-11% CAGR till FY30), propelled by increasing health awareness, a focus on preventive healthcare, higher disposable incomes, and evolving lifestyle trends. While challenges like consumer awareness gaps and regulatory clarity persist, ongoing FSSAI efforts to strengthen claim verification and streamline processes are positive. This growth in health-related products and services aligns with the wellness sub-segment within Consumer Services.

viewpoints.title: Heritage tourism is a key catalyst for sustainable development and economic growth
viewpoints.description: Heritage is a vital asset for India, driving sustainable development, cultural preservation, and economic growth through tourism. Modern travelers seek immersive, authentic, and meaningful experiences, demanding compelling storytelling and technology integration. Heritage tourism has immense potential to showcase India's civilizational legacy, create livelihoods, and foster inclusive growth across regions. Collaborative action among policymakers, industry, and stakeholders is crucial to unlock this wealth and enhance destination competitiveness.
viewpoints.source_title: Heritage reimagined: Driving immersive, tech-enabled and experience-led tourism

viewpoints.title: Heritage tourism transformation requires tech-enabled, experience-driven destination development
viewpoints.description: Global heritage tourism is transitioning from preservation-focused to experience-driven, with success increasingly dependent on immersive visitor engagement. India, with its extensive heritage, must adopt integrated, technology-enabled models to unlock its full potential. Leveraging advancements like AR/VR and AI for interpretation, accessibility, and management can enrich experiences. The future lies in balancing conservation with innovation, creating dynamic and competitive heritage destinations that encourage longer stays and higher spending.
viewpoints.source_title: Heritage reimagined: Driving immersive, tech-enabled and experience-led tourism

viewpoints.title: India's tourism and hospitality poised for substantial growth driven by diverse demand
viewpoints.description: India's travel and tourism sector is a robust economic contributor, generating significant GDP and employment, underpinned by diverse attractions and strong demand. Government policies, infrastructure investments, and new policy rollouts are strengthening the sector. Domestic and international traveler spending is expected to triple by 2034. Emerging segments like rural, spiritual, eco, luxury, adventure, medical, heritage, cruises, and camping, alongside AI/digital platforms, will drive a 'golden cycle' of growth.
viewpoints.source_title: Tourism And Hospitality Industry In India

demand_drivers.description: Travel inspiration is continuous and embedded in daily life through social feeds, film, TV, editorial content, reviews, and AI. 60% of travelers get trip ideas from social media.
68% of travelers view trips as integral to their identity, leading to splurging on experiences (52% Gen Z, 47% Millennials).
63% of travelers prefer curated lists of 10 recommended options over 500 options or a single AI-generated plan, valuing clear reasons for selection and control.

pnl_drivers.description: Customer reviews and authentic user-generated content increase confidence and conversion rates more effectively than purely curated brand narratives.
Lack of context sharing across multiple research tools and platforms creates friction, leading travelers to repeat searches and potentially abandon trips. Unsolved continuity increases churn risk.

new_opportunities.description: 71% of travelers are comfortable using AI for inspiration, and 86% would consider AI bookings in the future, signaling a readiness for AI-powered planning tools.
new_opportunities.opportunity: AI for travel inspiration and booking

new_opportunities.description: Half of travelers change booked accommodations after seeing better options, indicating an opportunity for active post-booking engagement and retention strategies.

Developing platforms that preserve traveler context across sessions/devices (saved content, preferences, rejected options) and offer resolution layers to reconcile conflicting information can drive deeper engagement and reduce churn.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Platform design for continuity and confidence

market_sizing.methodology: Qualitative analysis of market dynamics, outlining the shift in travel planning behavior and the growing influence of social media and AI on trip inspiration and booking processes. The report highlights increased touchpoints and complexities in the customer journey.
market_sizing.source_title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices

demand_drivers.description: Consumers are expanding their view of fitness to overall wellbeing, including cardiovascular health, weight management, longevity, and mental health, increasing spending across various wellness categories.

Wellness spending accelerates during pivotal life moments such as youth sports participation, weight-loss journeys, and setting new fitness goals, creating targeted acquisition and trade-up opportunities.

new_opportunities.description: The rise of GLP-1s creates opportunities to acquire new consumers by offering adjacent wellness products and services (fitness, nutrition, recovery, coaching) supporting broader health goals.

Partnerships or proprietary capabilities in wearables can generate valuable data, inform personalized marketing, and offer training content/coaching, appealing to engaged consumers focused on performance and progress.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Integration with wearables and connected tech

new_opportunities.description: Activewear brands can build relevance with younger consumers by partnering with fast-growing fitness communities, workout formats, and athletic events that reinforce team identity and achievement.
Expanding product portfolios to support low-impact activity and recovery (e.g., specific apparel, partnerships with practitioners) serves underserved needs during periods of injury or healthy aging.

market_sizing.methodology: Projection of the global wellness economy's annual growth rate and its key categories, highlighting consumer spending shifts. It also discusses the share of activewear within wellness spending across different geographies.
market_sizing.source_title: As Wellness Spending Grows, Can Activewear Brands Seize the Opportunity?

demand_drivers.description: 65% of visitors cite professional and social connection as a primary motivation for attending events, underscoring the value of MICE as a venue for business networking.

new_opportunities.description: MICE delegates spend 2-3 times more per day and stay longer than leisure tourists, making business events a high-value tourism segment for host cities, particularly in emerging Tier 2/3 destinations.

market_sizing.methodology: Estimates for organized MICE activity in India based on primary survey and economic impact model.
market_sizing.source_title: Socio-economic impact of the Indian events and experiences industry

demand_drivers.description: A global shift towards the 'Experience Economy' means consumers increasingly value memorable experiences over physical products, driving demand for live events.

new_opportunities.description: Major concerts and festivals generate substantial downstream expenditure in accommodation, transport, dining, and shopping, far exceeding ticket sales. For every INR 100 spent on concert tickets, an additional INR 585 is spent on related services.

market_sizing.methodology: Estimate for organized live events in India based on primary survey and economic impact model.
market_sizing.source_title: Socio-economic impact of the Indian events and experiences industry

demand_drivers.description: Weddings are a major component of household consumption and drive economic activity across various supporting industries.

market_sizing.methodology: Approximate wedding-linked household expenditure in India.
market_sizing.source_title: Socio-economic impact of the Indian events and experiences industry

demand_drivers.description: Post-COVID, the industry shifted from niche wellness to essential daily health support, driven by increased awareness and adoption of preventive healthcare.
Persistent malnutrition and growth in lifestyle-related disorders drive demand for scientifically formulated products that bridge nutrition and pharmaceuticals.

demand_drivers.driver: Higher disposable incomes and digital platforms
demand_drivers.description: Increasing incomes and the expansion of online delivery platforms facilitate easier access and greater consumption of nutraceutical products.

new_opportunities.description: Increased acquisition of mid-sized nutraceutical brands by larger FMCG players reflects a strategic move to strengthen their health and wellness offerings.

market_sizing.methodology: Forecast for India's nutraceutical market, including dietary supplements, functional foods, and beverages. Based on an estimated market size of USD 29-30 billion in 2024, projected to reach USD 37-38 billion by 2026, and USD 55-57 billion by 2030.

demand_drivers.description: Travelers increasingly seek deeper connections with places, valuing cultural immersion, learning, authentic local interactions, and personal enrichment over conventional sightseeing.
Gen Z travelers prioritize sustainability and authenticity, willing to pay a premium for environmentally responsible products and services, driving demand for destinations with strong commitments.
Mature travelers (51-70) maintain strong interest in cultural experiences, while younger generations (31-50, millennials) accelerate growth by seeking immersive, authentic, and sustainable travel.

new_opportunities.description: Leveraging augmented reality, virtual reality, AI, digital twins, and gamification to enrich heritage interpretation, improve accessibility, and personalize visitor journeys.
Adaptive reuse of palaces and forts for heritage hotels, and development of low-carbon 'net-zero heritage circuits,' cater to high-yield and climate-conscious travelers.
Integrating heritage assets with storytelling, local culture, gastronomy, community participation (e.g., heritage walks, culinary trails, workshops) to encourage longer stays and higher spending.

market_sizing.methodology: Valuation of the global heritage tourism market, projected to grow to USD937 billion by 2033. It also details India's domestic and foreign tourist arrival figures and contributions to global tourism earnings.
market_sizing.source_title: Heritage reimagined: Driving immersive, tech-enabled and experience-led tourism

demand_drivers.description: Travelers are increasingly seeking meaningful experiences that engage them emotionally, intellectually, and personally, moving beyond mere products or services.
These demographics drive demand for distinctive, memorable, and shareable experiences, prioritizing local workshops, destination-specific activities, and hands-on cultural immersion.
Travelers share their journeys online, turning experiences into personal expression and social identity, which amplifies the demand for unique and shareable moments.

new_opportunities.description: Businesses can build long-term visitor loyalty by emphasizing experience design, focusing on authenticity and immersion to deepen engagement and satisfaction across heritage tourism sub-dimensions.

market_sizing.methodology: Projection of the global experiential travel market, detailing its expected growth to USD359.4 billion by 2035. The methodology links market growth to traveler preferences for immersive, authentic, and meaningful experiences, driven by both passive and active participation.
market_sizing.source_title: Heritage reimagined: Driving immersive, tech-enabled and experience-led tourism

demand_drivers.driver: Expanding middle class and young population
demand_drivers.description: India's growing middle class and digitally engaged youth drive leisure travel growth both domestically and internationally.
Increased economic prosperity allows for greater discretionary spending on travel and leisure, fueling demand across various tourism segments.
Domestic tourism remains a key driver, with urban Indians increasingly opting for shorter, experience-led breaks like wellness and adventure tourism.

pnl_drivers.description: A reduction of GST on hotel stays under Rs. 7,500 to 5% is expected to significantly fuel growth in the hospitality sector and boost domestic travel.

new_opportunities.description: Promotion of mountain, eco-nature, turtle, bird-watching trails, rural, spiritual, luxury, adventure, medical, heritage, cruise, and camping tourism to attract varied global and domestic traveler segments.
Expansion of medical tourism hubs and MICE promotion through the 'Meet in India' strategy and digital catalogues create new investment avenues and business travel opportunities.

Leveraging AI for personalized recommendations, seamless booking, and virtual tours, along with other digital platforms, transforms the sector by optimizing destination management and visitor experiences.
new_opportunities.opportunity: AI and digital platforms for enhanced experiences

new_opportunities.description: Indian airlines and hotels are accommodating pet owners, leading to a notable surge in flight and accommodation bookings (26-43% YoY increase), signaling an emerging niche market.

market_sizing.methodology: Projection for India's tourism and hospitality sector, driven by domestic and international traveler spending. Also includes projections for medical tourism market, cultural/heritage tourism potential, overall GDP contribution and employment figures.
market_sizing.source_title: Tourism And Hospitality Industry In India

demand_drivers.description: India is recognized for building a holistic medical tourism ecosystem offering cost-effective and high-quality healthcare services.

Foreign Tourist Arrivals (FTAs) in 2024 show significant contributions from older age groups (55-64 and 65+) likely drawn by India’s wellness, heritage, and spiritual tourism offerings, including medical purposes.

new_opportunities.description: The Union Budget 2026–27 introduced a scheme to support states in establishing five Regional Medical Hubs, aiming to position India as a global destination for medical and wellness tourism.

market_sizing.methodology: Valuation of the medical tourism sector in India, with a projection to nearly double to US$ 16 billion by 2030 at a CAGR of 13.23%.
market_sizing.source_title: Tourism And Hospitality Industry In India

demand_drivers.description: India's variations in customs, traditions, and philosophy across states make heritage tourism a strong proponent for uplifting local economies.

market_sizing.methodology: Estimated potential revenue for cultural and heritage tourism in India, identified as the top revenue generator attracting 59% of surveyed travelers.
market_sizing.source_title: Tourism And Hospitality Industry In India

demand_drivers.driver: Rising demand for inland waterway tourism
demand_drivers.description: River cruise tourism on India’s National Waterways witnessed strong growth, with voyages increasing from 371 in FY24 to 443 in FY25.

market_sizing.methodology: Anticipated growth in cruise passenger traffic in India, from 0.4 million to four million by 2032, with economic potential soaring from US$ 110 million to US$ 5.5 billion.
market_sizing.source_title: Tourism And Hospitality Industry In India

demand_drivers.driver: Rising health awareness and lifestyle shifts
demand_drivers.description: Post-pandemic, there's a strong growth in wellness tourism driven by increasing health consciousness and evolving lifestyle choices, with a focus on wellness packages.

Significant contributions from the 55–64 and 65+ age groups in foreign tourist arrivals suggest a growing interest among senior travelers drawn by India’s wellness, heritage, and spiritual tourism offerings.

market_sizing.methodology: Valuation of the global wellness tourism market, expected to grow to US$ 2,054.9 billion by 2034 at a CAGR of 7.97%. India’s wellness tourism could contribute US$ 18 billion to India's GDP by 2030.
market_sizing.source_title: Tourism And Hospitality Industry In India

demand_drivers.description: Destinations like Rishikesh are attracting visitors with activities such as river rafting, bungee jumping, and trekking.

new_opportunities.description: Government initiatives and partnerships with organizations like the Indian Mountaineering Foundation aim to enhance safety and promote investment in adventure tourism.
Launch of portals like ‘Go-Adventure’ aim to streamline licensing and position regions as leading adventure tourism hubs.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Streamlining licensing and ease of doing business

market_sizing.methodology: India's ambition to transform its adventure tourism market into a US$ 800 billion market by 2047. Policy initiatives and safety standards are being strengthened to support this growth.
market_sizing.source_title: Tourism And Hospitality Industry In India

demand_drivers.description: Urban Indians increasingly prefer shorter, experience-led breaks, driving demand for outdoor activities like camping.

new_opportunities.description: The Ministry of Tourism has a policy for the development and promotion of caravan and caravan camping parks, supporting growth in this segment.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Promotion of camping sites and related infrastructure

market_sizing.methodology: Projected revenue of India’s camping market, expected to grow to Rs. 12,393 crore (US$ 1.45 billion) by 2030 at an annual rate of 14.32% between 2025 and 2030.
market_sizing.source_title: Tourism And Hospitality Industry In India
